A Sparse SDF VQ-VAE quantizes near-surface features while retaining explicit coordinates, using reconstruction supervision for surface fidelity and detail. 3D Byte-Pair Encoding (3D-BPE) merges recurring face-adjacent patterns using relative offsets before serialization. Macro tokens expand exactly into leaf tokens and coordinates. After Morton serialization, a shared LLM reads geometry for captioning and predicts tokens that decode into meshes for text-conditioned generation. With fixed geometry, architecture, and band width in voxels, sparse encoder cost grows approximately quadratically with resolution. 3D-BPE reduces mean complete LLM sequence length by 45.4 percent, including coordinates, text, and control tokens. SPAC achieves strong results in both 3D captioning and text-conditioned mesh generation. Ablations show gains over leaf tokens and Morton 1D-BPE in both tasks. The project page at https://yangjj007.github.io/spac/ .

candidates.title: Ads for Agents: Measuring Ad-Serving MCP Servers
candidates.abstract: AI agents call external tools through protocols such as the Model Context Protocol (MCP). Some MCP servers return paid advertisements (ads) into the model's context. The model then decides whether these ads and their disclosures reach the user. We trace these ads from their sources to the agent's tool results across public MCP servers and packages. We find the servers through their public traces in ad networks, package registries, certificate logs, hostnames, MCP directories, and GitHub configurations. We then query the ad-serving servers with read-only requests and inspect their ad links. Ads appear on only 0.57% of 101,363 open MCP endpoints and 0.04% of 122,656 local MCP packages. Although 173 ad networks target agents, operators insert the ads themselves on about half of the 226 ad-returning servers. Nearly all ad-serving packages likewise carry the operator's own affiliate identifier. While ads adapt to the topic and intent of the query, their disclosure stays fixed within each tool. Only 9.3% of the ads carry an explicit sponsored label. Most ad links also hide their destinations. Since operators insert most ads themselves and label them inconsistently, we propose a per-item ad annotation in MCP results. Clients can show this annotation to the user independently of the model's answer.

candidates.title: STRIDE: Strategy-to-Tactics Retrieval-Guided Skill Disclosure and Evolution for Agentic Reinforcement Learning
candidates.abstract: Skill-augmented reinforcement learning enables LLM agents to reuse task-solving knowledge across episodes, but existing systems typically expose agents to a flat skill pool and update skills only from coarse, episode-level outcomes. This conflates two distinct uses of experience: a stable strategy that should frame the whole episode, and tactical know-how that should be retrieved only when the agent reaches a local execution gap. We propose STRIDE (Strategy-to-Tactics Retrieval-guided skIll Disclosure and Evolution), a framework that brings progressive skill disclosure into agentic reinforcement learning. STRIDE keeps the selected strategy visible as episode context, exposes a compact tactic menu, and loads full tactic content only after an explicit retrieval action. This interface turns each retrieval into an event-level credit unit: the same event provides process feedback for learning when to retrieve and supplies evidence for skill-bank evolution. On ALFWorld, STRIDE achieves a 92.7% average success rate with Qwen3-4B and a 94.9% average success rate with Qwen3-8B. On WebShop, it improves over the strongest reproduced skill-augmented baseline by 4.5 score points and 1.9 success-rate percentage points. These results show that skill reuse is most effective when persistent strategies preserve global task structure and tactics are disclosed only at local decision bottlenecks.

candidates.title: StudioBench: Benchmarking Agentic Multimodal Large Language Models for Productive Audiovisual Creation
candidates.abstract: Video generators can now render convincing short clips, yet complete audiovisual works require coordinating visuals, sound, and editing across multiple stages. Existing benchmarks focus on individual generators or video agents under narrower production settings, leaving end-to-end creation by general multimodal large language models (MLLMs) underexplored. We introduce StudioBench, a benchmark comprising 160 tasks across eight video genres and five task types, spanning diverse audiovisual production requirements. Models produce minutes of finished audiovisual content using 33 atomic generation, editing, and inspection tools, without shell access or workflow templates. We evaluate the delivered films, while analyzing reconstructed workflow graphs to characterize production behavior and diagnose failures. Across seven MLLMs, explicit requirements are nearly saturated, yet production quality varies substantially in picture clarity and composition, object structure, motion, and lip sync. All models spontaneously organize multi-stage production workflows without predefined templates. However, higher-quality models exhibit more selective production workflows, whereas additional tool calls alone show little association with quality. These findings identify the missing quality loop of effective inspection, selection, and revision as a key bottleneck in productive audiovisual creation.

candidates.title: Gaze Graphs: A Scene-Level Representation of Visual Attention in the Operating Room
candidates.abstract: Purpose: Analyzing clinicians' visual attention from exocentric camera views can support surgical scene understanding without requiring wearable eye trackers. However, existing gaze-following research in the operating room (OR) estimates only 2D gaze locations without identifying attended scene entities or localizing gaze targets in 3D space. In this work, we investigate gaze graphs as a scene-level representation of visual attention that connects clinicians to attended scene entities, and evaluate their utility for fine-grained surgical action recognition and semantic scene graph (SSG) generation. Methods: We extend the public EgoExOR dataset with gaze annotations to create EgoExOR-Gaze, the first benchmark for multi-view gaze graph generation in the OR. We propose a novel architecture that jointly estimates 3D gaze targets and predicts attended entities using only exocentric camera views. Specifically, our approach exploits 3D gaze geometry to sample local visual features across multiple views for attended entity prediction. We further utilize predicted gaze graphs for fine-grained surgical action recognition and SSG generation. Results: For gaze graph generation, our model outperforms both exocentric-only and combined exocentric-egocentric baselines. For surgical action recognition, our model incorporating predicted gaze graphs outperforms both exocentric and egocentric baselines across all evaluated metrics, with particularly strong gains in temporal metrics. For SSG generation, incorporating gaze graphs improves macro-F1 from 0.42 to 0.52 compared to exocentric inputs alone, although performance remains below that achieved with egocentric inputs. Conclusion: Our results demonstrate the value of gaze graphs for surgical action recognition and SSG generation, highlighting the importance of explicitly modeling scene-level visual attention even when egocentric views are unavailable.

candidates.title: Topological Neural Collapse
candidates.abstract: Neural collapse (NC) predicts that, late in training, last-layer class features concentrate at their means and the means form a simplex equiangular tight frame (ETF). We ask whether NC also leaves a signature in the functional connectome of each layer: the graph of Pearson correlations between hidden-unit activations, built per class and summarized by persistent graph homology. Using deep MLPs, we observe two topological phenomena that co-occur with the well-studied geometric NC in the final layers during the terminal phase. Contrary to NC1, the split-half variability of a class connectome increases (TNC1). The mean pairwise $H_0$ distance $\bar{D}$ between class connectomes also rises (TNC2), but unevenly across class pairs, unlike the equidistance of NC2. We find that 24-56% of last-layer units become dead for some classes yet stay active for others, which inflates $\bar{D}$. After correcting for these units, both signatures remain elevated. These results from MNIST, Fashion-MNIST, CIFAR-10, and CIFAR-100 provide preliminary evidence that a topological mechanism may accompany the geometric signatures of NC.

candidates.title: A feasible point method for derivative-free linearly constrained optimization
candidates.abstract: This paper presents a framework for linearly constrained derivative-free optimization (DFO) in which the original objective function is evaluated only at feasible points. The method first analyzes the linear constraint system using certificates of infeasibility and implied activity to detect infeasibility or a singleton feasible set, or, when the feasible set has positive dimension, to identify the affine subspace spanned by the feasible set and obtain an equivalent reduced representation with a strictly feasible base point. It then transforms the resulting reduced problem into an unconstrained optimization problem by means of a pointed feasible retraction and an exact penalty function. The retraction maps arbitrary trial points to feasible points by an explicit scaling in the reduced coordinates, so that no constrained optimization or projection subproblem is required during objective evaluations. This construction permits a broad range of unconstrained DFO methods to be used as inner solvers while preserving feasibility of the original objective evaluations. Numerical experiments compare several such variants on linearly constrained test problems of different dimensions. The results show that the choice of inner solver affects robustness, the number of problems solved, function-evaluation efficiency, and computational time, and that relative performance changes with problem dimension.

candidates.title: Controlled One-Click Benchmarking and Post-Fusion Recalibration for Support-Conditioned Medical Segmentation
candidates.abstract: Sparse-prompt medical segmentation is hard to compare when prompts, supports, thresholds, and splits differ. This paper uses a controlled one-click protocol: each test image receives one positive foreground click, training-only support, validation-only checkpoint selection, and no test-time threshold tuning. We propose {Support-Aware Recalibration (SAR)}, a late post-fusion recalibration block for MultiverSeg that combines large-kernel spatial gating with squeeze-and-excitation channel recalibration after support--query fusion. BUSI, NerveUS-BP-present, and Kvasir-SEG are evaluated with matched 697 foreground-present sample budgets, shared splits/clicks, and threshold-free Dice-AUC/IoU-AUC. Compared with a protocol-matched raw-support MultiverSeg baseline, the main SAR configuration shows favorable mean Dice-AUC/IoU-AUC performance on BUSI, NerveUS-BP-present, and Kvasir-SEG, while reducing logged training time in this implementation. These controlled results indicate that late post-fusion recalibration is useful under a leakage-controlled one-click protocol.

candidates.title: FormaFin: Verifiable Financial Analysis with Solver-Guided Reinforcement Learning
candidates.abstract: Formally verifying financial analyses generated by large language models (LLMs) remains challenging as financial rules are largely expressed in natural language and rarely have corresponding formal specifications. Training language models to formalize these rules is hindered by the scarcity of labeled data and reliable training signals, while confidential financial data favor small models that run locally. We introduce FormaFin, a framework that trains small open language models to translate financial rules into reusable SMT formulas. FormaFin integrates teacher distillation with reinforcement learning using an SMT solver to compute rewards from numerical thresholds stated in financial rules. We evaluate FormaFin on corporate loan monitoring, in which lenders check borrowers' financial figures against loan agreements. To evaluate our framework, we curate \bench{}, a benchmark containing 143 loan agreements and 2,527 questions covering compliance, earnings cushion, and debt capacity. Our results show that a 7B formalizer achieves 94.8\% accuracy, outperforming open LLMs up to ten times larger. Across three model families, accuracy ranges from 92.6 to 96.8\%. Our framework also detects 95.6 to 99.7\% of errors in other LLMs' financial analyses. We make FormaFin and \bench{} publicly available.

candidates.title: A Novel Approach to Clustering Shape Data Using Iteratively Weighted Vectors with k-Means
candidates.abstract: Topological data analysis provides a collection of methods for analyzing data with shape structure, including point clouds, graphs, and images. Recent advances in topological vectorization have enabled the embedding of shape data into Euclidean spaces, facilitating comparisons and machine learning tasks. Vector summaries that effectively capture topological structures are particularly useful for shape classification and unsupervised learning tasks such as clustering. We investigate the use of vectorized topological data for clustering through k-means, which partitions observations into a fixed number of groups by minimizing a squared-error loss function. By incorporating an element-wise weight-update step into the iterative k-means algorithm, we improve clustering performance on both simulated and real-world shape datasets. We show that estimating these weights reduces to a least-squares problem, requiring minimal additional computation while allowing flexible coefficient constraints. Our approach also substantially strengthens the negative correlation between the loss and clustering accuracy, improving the effectiveness of selecting among multiple clustering solutions based on the lowest loss. These improvements remain robust to changes in vector length and the number of initializations. Furthermore, weighted topological vector summaries exhibit stability under small structural perturbations, particularly when weight constraints are imposed. The proposed method offers a flexible alternative for clustering topological data, accommodating different k-means variants, vectorization methods, and weight constraints.

candidates.title: Eidetic Code World Model
candidates.abstract: Executable code can preserve a world's structural layout, yet video renderers frequently alter the appearance of previously visited places once they leave the camera view. We present Paintress, a code-conditioned world model that couples an executable geometric proxy with an independently parameterized 3D Gaussian appearance memory in a shared metric coordinate frame. While the proxy enforces structural and visibility constraints, 3D Gaussians capture the visual realization synthesized by emitted observations. To balance stable incremental fusion with consistent readout, Paintress separates writing from reading: newly emitted frames update a persistent raw Gaussian map under confidence-gated selection, whereas a cloned reader copy is globally refined against the observation archive and rendered with coverage masks to condition generation. We also introduce Expedition-33, a benchmark for generated-appearance retention across 11 static scenes, five route families, and 15, 30, and 60 s target absences (165 settings per system). Excluded from the opening image, targets are synthesized during a shared prefix and scored against each system's own first visit at matched return cameras. Across ten systems (1,650 videos), Paintress achieves 0.1220 ROI-LPIPS, 0.0613 MAE, and 52.12% detail retention (vs. 0.2731, 0.1401, and 10.91% for CWM), with lower discrepancy at 60 s (0.1630) than CWM, AgentGarten, and Lyra 2.0 achieve at 15 s.

candidates.title: Correlation-aware sequential sampling for multi-output polynomial chaos expansions
candidates.abstract: The interaction of multiple physical processes in complex engineering systems is often characterized by several quantities of interest (QoIs) with non-negligible cross-correlations. Accurate uncertainty quantification of these responses requires repeated model evaluations, which can be computationally expensive. As an alternative, polynomial chaos expansion (PCE) provides an efficient surrogate modeling framework for reducing this computational cost owing to its natural structure for statistical analysis, while adaptive sequential sampling can further improve sampling efficiency under a limited model evaluation budget. However, adaptive sampling strategies specifically designed for multi-output PCE remain limited, and existing approaches commonly aggregate information from individual outputs without explicitly accounting for their statistical dependence. When strong correlations exist among QoIs, output-wise aggregation can give greater combined influence to response patterns shared by several outputs. To reduce the influence of such repeated representation on sample allocation, this study develops a principal component analysis-based extension of the multi-output criterion for adaptive construction of PCE. The sampling criterion combines component-wise normalization with the retention of selected principal directions, thereby adjusting the relative influence of shared response patterns while preserving distance-based exploration. The method is verified through numerical examples with different levels of output coupling and is compared with the conventional multi-output criterion and reference sampling strategies. The results demonstrate that accounting for output dependence improves the allocation of new samples among multiple response features and enhances the efficiency of multi-output PCE surrogate construction, particularly for strongly correlated QoIs.

candidates.title: Beyond Invoice Volumes: Temporal Network Structure, Maturity Concentration, and Systemic Liquidity Exposure in SME Trade-Credit Networks
candidates.abstract: Trade-credit invoices encode directed obligations whose temporal synchronization and counterparty concentration are obscured by annual volume totals. We audit 749,952 atomic B2B invoices from 2012-2023 (EUR 99.705B; 75,343 firms) from the pseudonymized Mendeley Data corpus (Esteva de la Rosa, 2026), separating 1,240 terminal 2024 bridge records (EUR 630.12M; 9 bridge-only firms) and 13 extreme-duration contracts (>3,650 days; EUR 297.75k). Using directed weighted graphs, HHI, Shannon entropy, CR1 shares, spectral centralities, and multi-cadence temporal operators, we formulate and benchmark a Maturity-Aware Network Exposure (MANE) indicator. Invoice values are heavily skewed: the top 1% hold 81.41% of value (Gini = 0.9742). Two-way fixed-effects panels with circular block bootstrapping ($B=999$, 12-month blocks) and Holm-Bonferroni control show higher lagged debtor counterparty concentration is associated with lower MANE ($\hatβ=-0.494$, 95% CI $[-0.752,-0.248]$, $p_{\mathrm{Holm}}=0.004$). Robustness audits (R1-R4) confirm stability under 2021 exclusion ($-0.402$, $p=0.004$), Shannon entropy ($+0.257$), CR1 ($-0.515$), 1%-99% Winsorization ($-0.462$, all $p=0.001$), and multi-invoice debtors (count $\ge 2$, $-0.334$, $p=0.031$). Conversely, within-FE diagnostics expose severe joint-concentration multicollinearity (VIF = 22.22) that vanishes for multi-invoice debtors ($p=0.719$), while regime splits reveal a macro reciprocity sign reversal between 2012-2019 ($-0.706$) and 2020-2023 ($+0.232$, both $p=0.001$). In 12-month purged forecasting, MANE does not reliably improve over maturity seeds ($Δ\mathrm{MSE}=2.668$, 95% CI $[-0.027,7.954]$; trimmed $0.067$, $[-0.035,0.194]$), positioning MANE as a reproducible screening and auditing diagnostic, rather than a default proxy, for supply-chain finance, multilateral clearing, and RWA tokenization.

candidates.title: NAT: Scaling Causal Neural Action Tokenizers Across Embodiments
candidates.abstract: Action tokenizers let robot policies treat control as autoregressive next-token prediction. As these policies are trained on larger and more diverse datasets, they will need a universal tokenizer that can encode actions from many embodiments and data sources, including ones it has not seen. We study action tokenization at scale, training on 49k hours of action data from real-world robots, handheld grippers, simulation, and humans. We introduce Neural Action Tokenizer (NAT), a causal tokenizer whose decoder lets actions be executed as their tokens are generated. Across four simulation benchmarks, NAT outperforms FAST and prior neural action tokenizers when tokenizing unseen robot embodiments, and in vision-language-action models it outperforms FAST+ across four benchmarks and on a real robot when acting through its tokens. NAT tokens also close the performance gap to a flow-matching action head on some benchmarks while lowering the inference latency for first actions. Our experiments also find that robot data may not be necessary to learn an effective action space: a NAT trained only on human hand motion performs close to tokenizers trained on robot data.

candidates.title: SENSA: Visual-to-Brain Generation with Individualized Subject-State Transfer and Adaptation
candidates.abstract: Visual-to-brain encoding predicts neural responses to visual stimuli, supporting visual cognition research and neural decoding. However, challenges in disentangling shared from image-specific activity, together with inter-subject distribution shifts and representational heterogeneity, limit accurate encoding and cross-subject generalization with limited calibration data. We introduce SENSA, a structured continuous neural response generation framework that separates shared activity from image-dependent responses and calibrates a compact subject state. An independent response prior captures shared activity, while complementary visual descriptors drive separable sensor-time bases and a shared Response Refiner. Subject-Adaptive Factor Transport adjusts the spatiotemporal expression of shared bases, while Source-Grounded Residual Memory predicts image-dependent corrections in source-response coordinates. Together, they personalize a frozen generator using limited paired support. Experiments demonstrate that the generation backbone outperforms recent generators across three datasets, with image-identity perturbations confirming stimulus specificity. Using only 400 paired images, electroencephalography (EEG) and the Natural Scenes Dataset (NSD) calibration achieve residual Pearson correlations of 0.1091 and 0.2995, respectively, demonstrating effective brain-response generation and cross-subject adaptation.

candidates.title: KineState-SWAM: A Surgical World Action Model with Explicit Kinematics and Causal Interaction Dynamics
candidates.abstract: Existing surgical world models often leave implicit how instrument motion drives localized tissue responses and how interaction history informs subsequent actions. We introduce KineState-SWAM, a surgical world-action model coupling action prediction and video generation through a persistent interaction state, separating kinematically determined instrument motion from learned scene evolution. A flow-matching policy predicts joint trajectories conditioned on interaction state, robot configuration, and task instruction. Kinematic Geometry Conditioning converts these trajectories into surface-motion tokens and spatially aligned instrument renderings using calibrated URDF kinematics. Causal Interaction Dynamics recurrently updates the state through geometry-guided attention and motion-aligned feature transport, carrying interaction history into subsequent action predictions without intermediate video synthesis. The State-Geometry Adapter combines state-dependent spatial modulation with localized geometric residuals to guide video generation. Interaction-aware supervision emphasizes tissue responses near instrument working regions. We introduce dVRK-Chole5.2k, comprising 5,255 videos spanning 17 surgical tasks. Experiments demonstrate improved action accuracy and video fidelity over evaluated baselines within matched action-conditioning settings. Ablations support preserving and transporting interaction states for long-horizon prediction.

candidates.title: Thakaa at StanceEval-2026: Inference-Time Target Grounding for Arabic Stance Detection
candidates.abstract: StanceEval-2026 tests Arabic stance classification under target shift, with evaluation targets absent from the labelled task data. We test two ways to supply target information at inference time. For Track 1, we retrieve eight labelled Women Driving demonstrations from the external ArabicStanceX corpus and score the three label tokens with Gemma-4-31B-IT. For the unseen-target track, we prepend cached target context prompted to be factual and non-evaluative, then fuse label predictions and label-token scores from multiple LLMs, with final assignments constrained by published class totals. The systems obtain 85.22 and 91.78 Favg2 on Tracks 1 and 2, ranking sixth and fourth in the final standings. On held-out ArabicStanceX tweets, direct prompting scores 79.45 Favg2; eight random Women Driving demonstrations raise it to 84.78, and similarity retrieval reaches 89.04. Across three target-held-out Mawqif evaluations, a fixed target card raises Gemma-4-31B-IT from 86.54 to 86.93, whereas QLoRA lowers Gemma-4-12B-IT from 84.43 to 83.77. In these separate public evaluations, same-target demonstrations and retrieval improve performance, factual target context provides small, target-dependent gains, and the tested source-only adapter does not improve.

candidates.title: Interaction Retention and Output-Likelihood Training in Parallel Sampling
candidates.abstract: Parallel samplers such as masked diffusion language models generate several coordinates per step from conditional marginals and randomize which coordinates are generated together, so even exact conditionals return a distorted distribution. We give an exact local account of this distortion. Around any full-support product law, the Gram operator of the sampler's response is diagonal in the interaction decomposition, and its eigenvalues are retention probabilities: the probability that an interaction has a unique latest-revealed coordinate. This retention spectrum determines the exact frontier between output accuracy and conditional calibration, its regularization path, and the population response of finite-mixture likelihood training. For pairwise interactions it yields a sharp dichotomy. Under homogeneous retention, output-likelihood training is equivalent to a single context gain; heterogeneous retention opens correction directions beyond any scalar, with an advantage bounded by an explicit heterogeneity gap. On binarized digits and MNIST, output-likelihood training within a heterogeneous schedule library lowers calibrated test negative log-likelihood in all twelve paired comparisons, and the gain survives pair-specific recalibration and a stronger path optimizer. For a frozen 169.6-million-parameter masked diffusion language model, serially normalized context gains are 1.070 and 1.056 at 8 and 16 rounds, against the predicted values 1.134 and 1.058.

candidates.title: Thakaa at AlexandriaX-2026: Who Gets the Final Say? Assigning Output Authority in Dialectal Arabic Machine Translation and Error Detection
candidates.abstract: We report first-place systems for all four evaluated AlexandriaX-2026 settings: both English-to-dialect translation tracks, cross-dialect translation, and translation-error detection. In unconstrained translation, our minimum Bayes risk (MBR) selection restricts output authority: four local systems can supply the translation, while seven additional systems contribute only reference evidence. Candidate-constrained MBR beats the strongest complete candidate in all 13 dialects and gains 1.2554 macro spBLEU overall, reaching 33.4891. It also surpasses a retrospective oracle selecting the best whole candidate system per dialect. In the constrained track, country-routed LoRA adapters over a shared NileChat-3B-Base backbone incorporate the released Libyan and Sudanese supervision absent from the training and development splits, raising macro spBLEU from 29.5969 to 30.4233. Post-evaluation, a single adapter trained on all released Alexandria data reaches 30.4733 macro spBLEU; averaging model weights across three training seeds raises this to 30.9726 while retaining one model for inference. For cross-dialect translation, nonparallel target-dialect retrieval guides deliberation, raising Gemma-4-31B-IT without fine-tuning from 24.6898 to 28.4011 spBLEU. For translation-error detection, GPT-5.5 proposes semantic error regions, while MARBERTv2 controls their character boundaries and corroborates additional spans, raising Overall from 0.4691 to 0.4982.

candidates.title: PhyMind: Physics-Informed Masked Autoencoding for EEG Foundation Models
candidates.abstract: EEG foundation models are pre-trained almost exclusively with masked reconstruction through a free-form decoder, sometimes with hand-crafted spectral targets added, as in MANAS-2. We study what happens when that decoder is replaced by a generative forward model of EEG. PhyMind keeps a standard masked transformer encoder, but its decoder must explain the masked signal through 68 cortical regions, each driven by damped stochastic oscillators and an aperiodic Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process, projected to the recording's own montage by a fixed boundary-element lead field evaluated per derivation. Training combines masked reconstruction with a Whittle spectral likelihood, an oscillator-dynamics residual, a minimum-norm source prior and a penalised neural residual. In a controlled comparison (same encoder, data, steps and seed), the physics decoder produces encoder tokens whose spectral content is far more linearly decodable than with a masked-autoencoder decoder or with the MANAS-2 objective: mean R^2 on a token-level spectral probe with amplitude-normalised targets is 0.67/0.77/0.77 on three datasets, against 0.24/0.50/0.50 (MAE) and 0.48/0.67/0.66 (MANAS-2 objective), approaching the released 92.8M-parameter MANAS-2 (0.71/0.81/0.80). Downstream gains in the controlled setting are small (four-task mean balanced accuracy 56.6 vs. 53.8 for MAE frozen, 63.8 vs. 62.7 fine-tuned). Region-level features from the physics decoder raise frozen four-class motor-imagery accuracy by 7-14 points, so a 7.2M-parameter model pre-trained on 3k hours of open EEG is comparable to the released MANAS-2 with frozen features (63.0 vs. 61.6). After full fine-tuning, MANAS-2 remains better (66.8 vs. 65.4 for our best model). The inferred sources do not reproduce the lateralisation that a classical inverse solution finds in motor imagery, so we do not claim anatomical interpretability. Code and weights are released.

candidates.title: Dynamic Model Merging with Multi-Layer Aggregated Routing Evidence
candidates.abstract: Dynamic model merging aims to retain the efficiency of a unified model while better preserving task-specific expertise through input-dependent routing at both the task and head levels. However, even the routing components of the state-of-the-art approach remain limited: the task routing is highly sensitive to the choice of routing layer, whereas the head routing relies on simple max-logit competition. To address these limitations, we propose multi-layer aggregated routing evidence (MATE) as a unified mechanism for improving both task and head routing. Specifically, we first introduce a metric to quantify task routing separability across different layers. Empirical analysis of this metric reveals that different layers provide complementary evidence for identifying the tasks relevant to an input. Motivated by this observation, MATE selects multiple informative layers according to their routing separability and aggregates their layer-wise routing scores to produce a more robust signal that can be directly used for task selection. Moreover, we observe that this signal also encodes useful information about the suitability of the corresponding classification heads. This motivates us to further combine the MATE signal with the max-logit score to guide classification head selection. Extensive experiments on vision benchmarks demonstrate that MATE consistently achieves state-of-the-art performance.

candidates.title: Bias Cascade: Understanding the Gap Between Knowledge Alignment and Effect Replication in LLM-based Social Simulation
candidates.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to simulate participants in social experiments. Existing research has primarily focused on aligning social knowledge and isolated responses, while overlooking whether simulations can reproduce the collective effects of social interventions. This distinction is critical due to a failure mechanism we call a $bias$ $cascade$: similar individual states can lead to different actions, while agreement on isolated actions can still produce divergent outcomes through dynamic interactions. As a result, models may produce accurate social judgments yet fail to reproduce the outcomes of classic human studies. To investigate this problem empirically, we introduce $REFLEX$ (Reproducing Effects of Foundational Literature EXperiments), a benchmark of 30 counterfactual social experiments grounded in classic human studies that compares knowledge judgment with effect simulation. Knowledge judgment directly predicts the direction of an intervention's effect, whereas effect simulation fixes the scenario and participants while varying one prespecified social factor, with agents generating actions from local observations that are aggregated into macro-level average treatment effects. Compared with human-study findings, the best-performing model achieves net directional scores of 0.847 for knowledge judgment and 0.453 for effect simulation. Moreover, longer causal chains are associated with poorer effect replication, consistent with the bias-cascade hypothesis. These findings reveal a substantial gap between knowledge alignment and effect replication, showing that current methods remain inadequate for reliably simulating collective human behavior.

candidates.title: CivilCADBench: Benchmarking Multimodal LLMs for Understanding, Reconstructing, and Designing Civil Engineering Drawing Sets
candidates.abstract: Civil infrastructure is designed, built, and maintained through engineering drawing sets, yet preparing and revising them remains labour-intensive and calls for automation. Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) are promising candidates, but assessing them requires a benchmark grounded in real engineering practice. We introduce CivilCADBench, a benchmark for understanding, reconstructing, and designing civil engineering drawing sets, built from real infrastructure drawings and source CAD files containing over 250,000 CAD entities. Unlike parametric 3D CAD models, these drawings are dense, layered, and multi-sheet; and since prints are lossy projections with no pixel trace of layers, a file can print correctly yet remain wrongly organised. CivilCADBench comprises three task families of increasing difficulty: understanding tasks are evaluated with 2,183 expert-reviewed questions ranging from single sheets to whole sets, while reconstruction and design tasks are agentic, requiring models to rebuild printed pages as editable CAD files, either as single pages or entire drawing sets, and to produce new designs. These tasks are performed across 232 pages, 28 sets, and 19 design tasks, and evaluated by a deterministic scorer that compares model outputs with the designers' source files on geometry, layers, text, and dimensions. We evaluate seven frontier MLLMs on CivilCADBench, and find that they read and redraw printed content accurately but recover the file structure poorly: the best model scores above 90% in understanding and single-page reconstruction, yet only 60% on layer assignment and 48% on design. Grounded in real engineering practice, CivilCADBench exposes both the capabilities and the limitations of frontier models in professional civil engineering, laying a foundation for next-generation models and agentic systems for intelligent civil engineering.

candidates.title: MQCODet: Modality Quality-Guided Collaborative Optimization for UAV-Based RGB-T Tiny Pedestrian Detection
candidates.abstract: Unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV)-based RGB-thermal (RGB-T) remote sensing provides complementary visual and thermal information for pedestrian perception under complex aerial observation conditions. However, detecting tiny pedestrians in UAV-based RGB-T imagery remains challenging due to cross-modal spatial heterogeneity, manifested as modality quality imbalance and spatial position misalignment. Existing RGB-T detectors primarily address these challenges at the feature fusion stage, without establishing an effective coupling between feature fusion and object localization, potentially resulting in suboptimal detection performance. To address this limitation, we introduce a Modality Quality-Guided Collaborative Optimization Detector (MQCODet), which extends modality quality from a fusion prior to a localization supervision cue. Specifically, we propose a Dynamic Calibration and Region-Aware Fusion (DCRF) module that progressively refines cross-modal spatial alignment and performs region-aware fusion to generate reliable multi-scale features and a scene-level modality quality prior. We further design an Efficient Contextual Interaction (ECI) encoder to enhance multi-scale feature interaction while preserving fine-grained spatial details. Moreover, we propose a Modality-Aware Adaptive (MAA) loss that incorporates the modality prior and object scale to adaptively balance spatial consistency and geometric similarity for localization supervision. Extensive experiments demonstrate that MQCODet surpasses state-of-the-art methods on two UAV-based RGB-T tiny pedestrian detection benchmarks while achieving real-time inference on the edge platform.

candidates.title: Guarding with Judgment: Learning to Intervene for Multimodal Safety
candidates.abstract: When visual context makes an ordinary request unsafe to answer as asked, a blanket refusal may leave the user's need unresolved. Choosing how to help requires distinguishing an established hazard from a condition that still needs verification, a distinction that binary safety labels leave unspecified. We formulate this decision through four actions: allow, warn, review, and refuse. To ground these decisions in verifiable evidence, we build a corpus of 20,126 training audits and the JudiBench benchmark, connecting each action to diagnostic judgments, source evidence, and controlled context changes. Our guard, JudiAct, separately states what the source establishes, what condition governs the help, and how the rules apply. It then checks these three brief review items against the original inputs to predict diagnostic labels and a handling action. Supervised training learns individual judgments while comparing label assignments across related cases. A second stage swaps one review item at a time, using the resulting audit feedback to refine review generation. On JudiBench, JudiAct improves request and answer Macro-F1 by more than 28 percentage points over its 4B backbone. Across nine public benchmarks, it outperforms state-of-the-art guards on the mean delivered-answer score in both pre-generation and post-generation settings, cutting MM-SafetyBench attack success from 40.78% to 25.30%.

candidates.title: Twisted Block Particle Filters: A Local Particle-System Change of Measure for High-Dimensional State-Space Models
candidates.abstract: Block particle filters mitigate weight degeneracy in high-dimensional state-space models, but their normalizer estimates can remain highly variable. We introduce a twisted block particle filter (TBPF) that incorporates predictive guidance through an exact change of measure at blockwise resampling. The method guide-tilts one uniformly selected offspring per block, leaves the state-transition kernel unchanged, and computes the resampling correction using finite empirical guide averages. We prove that this correction exactly preserves the finite-particle block particle filter normalizer expectation, separating the effect of guided sampling from the approximation introduced by spatial blocking. Our analysis provides exact conditional local moments and a one-step conditional central limit result. We further derive explicit bounds on the correction accumulated across blocks and time, establish fixed-horizon consistency of the block filter and corrected normalizer under suitable regularity and guide-range conditions, and identify conditional criteria for guide perturbations that reduce variance. Experiments on coupled linear Gaussian and stochastic-volatility models with up to 256 latent dimensions show lower measured log-normalizer variance. For stochastic volatility with a five-step guide, the median reduction is $38\%$. An application to a 100-dimensional financial portfolio panel extends the evaluation to real data.

candidates.title: EA-Bench: Measuring information and action efficiency under imperfect instructions
candidates.abstract: Personal agents help users complete everyday work across digital applications. Many standard benchmarks assume that users provide sufficient information to solve a task. However, agents often encounter incomplete, distracting, or inconsistent information in practice. To systematically study agent inefficiency under such imperfect information, we introduce Efficient Action (EA)-Bench, which evaluates both tool calls and user interactions in work-related tasks. To our knowledge, it is the first benchmark to jointly evaluate tool-call efficiency and user-interaction efficiency under controlled missing, redundant, and conflicting information. We construct 63 base-task instances adapted from existing work-related benchmarks. To guide perturbation design and quantify task requirements, we represent workflows as directed acyclic graphs (DAGs) and examine node-level dependencies to identify where information can be withheld, contradicted, or supplemented with distractors. We use a two-stage validation process combining AI-assisted checks with expert screening to select 232 conditions from 792 initial candidates. We organize these tasks into Easy and Hard tracks by task complexity. Experiments show that imperfect information can reduce accuracy and increase tool-use and user-interaction costs. More concerning, several models obtain apparently correct outcomes by guessing user-specific values without confirmation, revealing potential execution unreliability in current models under imperfect user information.

candidates.title: AgriManager: A Framework and Benchmark for LLM-RL Generalization in Agricultural Management
candidates.abstract: Agricultural management is heterogeneous along two axes. The first is distributional shift within a fixed task interface: weather, crops, and prices vary across years and locations while sensors, actions, and objective stay fixed. The second is structural shift across interfaces: different farms expose different observed variables, available actions, and management objectives. We formalize the second axis as schema shift: variation in the policy-facing schema $Σ= (Σ_O, Σ_A, Σ_R)$ between training and deployment. We test whether LLM-RL generalizes across both axes with AgriManager, to our knowledge the first framework that trains LLM policies with RL across multiple process-based crop simulators, unifying DSSAT, WOFOST, and Cycles. We design a three-tier generalization ladder: Tier 1 within-schema distributional shift, Tier 2 single-axis schema shift along $Σ_O / Σ_A / Σ_R$, Tier 3 compositional schema shift across simulators, all scored on a frozen held-out test suite with three training seeds per method. Within fixed schemas, Qwen3-4B trained by RL with explicit reasoning exceeds neural-network PPO trained with the same interaction budget; without reasoning, training stalls near no-action where the reward penalizes input use. Under single-axis schema shift, $Σ_O$ transfer needs decision-critical state, $Σ_A$ results are consistent with joint action-menu coverage, and with reasoning a policy trained on yield alone transfers to unseen objectives. Under compositional schema shift, single-source training mostly hurts zero-shot transfer across simulators, and a unified policy trained only on other combinations of the same components recovers about 86% of the gain of a specialist trained on the target combination on DSSAT and stays below the specialists on the WOFOST and Cycles profit targets. Project page: https://agrimanager-framework.github.io

candidates.title: Learning How a Body Moves: Few-Shot Body Inference for Visual World Models of Animated Characters
candidates.abstract: Two visually identical animated characters can respond differently to the same action command because their body dynamics differ. For example, a stiff blob and its bouncy twin reach different heights when both receive the jump command. Given only the first frame and the action command, a visual world model has no information to distinguish these twins, because their initial appearances are identical. We therefore propose an in-context world model that encodes clips of a character's other actions into a body representation, using a contrastive loss to separate look-alike characters. We introduce ToonTwins, a benchmark of 144 2D cartoon characters that run, jump, fall, turn and crouch. Its characters form look-alike groups of four that differ only in their dynamics profile, and we also evaluate the model on 32 animated animals from DeformingThings4D. Even with a body code from these clips, the latent pixel world model we tested recovered at most 25 percent of the twins' jump height difference. On new shapes, our model identified the correct twin in 85.9 percent of cases, compared with 76.7 percent for a transformer baseline that reads the same clips without a body summary, and in a controlled ablation the contrastive loss gave more than half of this gain. On the animated animals, it reduced the mean path prediction error by 8.5 percent against a model without body information.

candidates.title: Task-Conditioned Detail Allocation for Synthetic Segmentation Data
candidates.abstract: Synthetic images sharing a segmentation label can differ in their training value. We propose Task-Conditioned Detail Allocation (TCDA) to select useful candidates and locally edit some remaining images. We ask whether image details provide class-specific cues in the regions marked by the label. We train a small task reference on frozen image features from real training images. We compare its class responses before and after blurring each candidate, and score how well these response changes align with the labeled regions. This detail allocation score ranks candidates from the same source. Comparing their response--label alignment with that of the real source image also guides repair decisions and, in multiclass tasks, the choice of regions to edit. Selected candidates and accepted repairs are used for training with the original labels and the unchanged downstream segmenter. Experiments on camouflaged object detection, degraded salient object detection, and adverse-condition semantic segmentation show that our selection outperforms equally sized random and label-agreement subsets. Combining selection and repair improves over real-only training by up to 0.019 in $S_α$ on COD10K and 2.86 mIoU points on ACDC.

candidates.title: Spatially Grounded Latent Lookahead for Vision-Language-Action Models
candidates.abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models benefit from strong semantic representations that support object recognition and instruction understanding. However, precise manipulation also depends on resolving object locations and workspace relations, and on selecting actions with an estimate of how the scene will evolve. Existing geometry-aware methods make the current scene more explicit, while predictive methods model future observations or representations. Yet future information is often neither grounded in a control-relevant spatial state nor directly used to guide action generation. We introduce Spatially Grounded Latent Lookahead (SG-LL), which uses the grounded present as the reference for predicting an actionable near-future representation. A frozen spatial teacher first distills geometric priors into policy-connected spatial tokens. A current-conditioned bottleneck then learns a compact latent that captures future information relative to the present scene. This latent is predicted from the current policy context and initial Action Expert features, without access to future observations or the spatial teacher. Finally, zero-initialized residual fusion incorporates the predicted latent into the Action Expert to refine action generation. Experiments on LIBERO-Plus, CALVIN, and three real-world manipulation tasks demonstrate improvements over in both simulation and real-robot settings.

candidates.title: Omni-H3-Image: Constrained Foundation Priors Usher in a New Era of All-in-One Blind Image Restoration
candidates.abstract: Off-the-shelf unified image models such as 33B MiniMax-H3-Image, FLUX.1-Kontext, and Qwen-Image-Edit-2511 synthesize crisp textures yet collapse to 11.33-16.74 dB PSNR across 429 degraded public restoration scenes due to spatial drift, chromatic hallucination, and semantic fabrication. We present Omni-H3-Image (Omni-H3), an approximate three-stage constrained posterior projection framework over unmodified MiniMax-H3-Image and Qwen3-VL-32B using only a 0.92M-parameter auxiliary weather pre-conditioner (<0.003% of backbone weights). Omni-H3 unifies blind physics-VLM sensing with exact-32 px lattice anchoring, joint affine-Wiener-Butterworth projection in opponent YCbCr space, and closed-loop Z=4 text verification with sub-Nyquist abstention. Across 925 blind tasks against 11 external SOTA baselines -- five public benchmarks (N=647), Dev-160, and a held-out locked_test suite (N=118) -- Omni-H3 recovers +4.73 dB degraded-scene PSNR over Base H3 (21.47 vs. 16.74 dB; +6.27-10.14 dB over other omni backbones) while winning overall #1 DISTS (0.207), #1 NIQE (4.45), and #1 Edge-F1 (0.807) on all 429 degraded public scenes (MUSIQ 66.8 vs. 40-44 for discriminative SOTA), 76.59 dB on CBSD68 Clean, -91.6% Urban100 chroma drift, #1 2K Dev Non-Clean DISTS (0.202), and #1 locked_test 2K DISTS (0.173) and 132-ROI SubCER, cutting pre-annotated 132-ROI SubCER from 0.456 to 0.319 under non-Qwen RapidOCR (PP-OCRv4) (with recognizer-dependent tradeoffs under TrOCR-large-str).

candidates.title: Operational Assurance for LLM-Based Systems under Governance Opacity
candidates.abstract: In the contemporary artificial intelligence ecosystem, foundation models are increasingly deployed under AI-as-a-Service (AIaaS) schemes characterized by high technical opacity, technological concentration, and limited external auditing capability over governance, training, and internal operational processes. Under these conditions, traditional ethical oversight approaches that focus exclusively on corporate governance or on internal model inspection become insufficient to ensure effective control over AI systems deployed in real-world contexts. This work proposes a pragmatic operational assurance framework inspired by Zero-Trust principles from cybersecurity, which shifts effective auditing efforts toward the application layer, where risk acquires observable, contextualized, and operationally verifiable properties. The proposal articulates two complementary evaluation levels: a black-box evaluation aimed at characterizing general behaviors, vulnerabilities, and risky capabilities of foundation models through conversational scanning, and a grey-box evaluation focused on the operational contextualization of risk within the actual deployment environment of the audited application. The framework incorporates mechanisms to move from general, CVSS-inspired severity metrics toward contextualized operational risk assessments that take into account user profiles, industrial domains, and organizational knowledge. In addition, the proposal strengthens practical auditability through digitally signed explainability reports (signed XAI reports), designed to support verifiable traceability, continuous monitoring, and operational accountability in LLM-based sociotechnical systems.

candidates.title: Self-WSP: Can Language Models Improve Themselves Through Weight-Space Programming?
candidates.abstract: Frontier language models can now read and edit the weights of a neural network much like code and thereby improve a small model, an approach known as Weight-Space Programming (WSP). We further explore applying WSP to a language model itself, which we call Self-WSP. Specifically, Qwen3.5-0.8B reads its own weights, proposes an edit, and then continues with the edited weights as both problem solver and editor. We find many cases of genuine self-improvement. Self-edits can raise GSM8K accuracy from 11.8% to 62.2% and MATH500 accuracy from 7.0% to 32.2%, sometimes by changing only 16 parameters, and in some cases repeated self-editing keeps improving the model. A closer look, however, reveals that these gains lack interpretability. The model shows little understanding of the edits it makes, and WSP driven by random search sometimes performs comparably. Self-WSP thus holds promise as a path toward recursive self-improvement (RSI), but realizing this promise requires further exploration.

candidates.title: Hidden Sensitivity in LLM Pre-training: A Dynamic System View
candidates.abstract: In Large Language Model (LLM) pre-training, loss curves can conceal substantial instability, i.e., even small perturbations may lead to dramatically different predictions while leaving loss nearly unchanged. To investigate this phenomenon and reveal the underlying mechanisms, we first formulate LLM pre-training as a non-autonomous dynamical system that jointly evolves model weights and Adam optimizer states. Based on this formulation, we introduce a normalized sensitivity score in optimizer-relative coordinates to identify sensitive training checkpoints. At one such checkpoint, a weight perturbation of only 10^(-5) leads to 35.7% disagreement in top-1 predictions and 16.2% disagreement in benchmark answers after 200 training steps, with only 0.8% of greedy generations remaining identical despite similar validation losses. Furthermore, we find that perturbations to Adam's first and second moments induce comparably large effects, with similar sensitivity patterns observed in OLMo-1B. Finally, guided by our diagnostic, targeted stabilization reduces top-1 disagreement to 0.83% and increases generation exact match to 88.3%, at the cost of a 0.11-nat increase in validation loss. Our findings reveal a hidden form of optimizer-state-dependent sensitivity in LLM pre-training that conventional loss-based evaluations may overlook, while demonstrating its potential for diagnosis and mitigation.

candidates.title: Does a Frontier Large Language Model Know What It Can Solve? A 100-Conjecture Calibration Study
candidates.abstract: How does confidence correlate with actual performance in large language models, when attacking open research-level math problems? We address this question by studying the performance of ChatGPT 5.6 Sol Ultra on a set of 100 open conjectures in geometric analysis. By construction, the model first selected open problems in geometric analysis that it assessed that it had at least a 50\% chance of proving or disproving, and then assigned a probability of success to each question. 13 questions were then excluded after an audit, and the model was asked to resolve the remaining 87 problems. Its mean stated resolution probability was $0.617$, versus an observed rate of $0.103$ (Brier score $0.351$, ECE $0.513$), thereby demonstrating that the model was systematically over-confident in its self-assessment. However, the scores retained ranking signal (AUROC $0.714$). The model was highly overconfident in probability magnitude but did more often than not assign a high probability of success to the problems that it did resolve, than the problems that it did not. Hence, its probabilities were numerically mis-calibrated but directionally correct. All proofs have been formalized in Lean, thereby verifying correctness, and have been run through a semantic equivalence pipeline to ensure semantic equivalence between the formalized and informal statements. These are exploratory campaign outcomes, not fixed-budget success probabilities. The certificates prove formal statements; for a couple of questions, some geometric inputs are assumed in the lean proofs.

candidates.title: More Is Never Less: Affordable Robustness to Additive Attacks via Monotone Multiple-Instance Learning
candidates.abstract: Static malware detectors that represent each sample as a bag of extracted features, such as permissions, API calls, or imported functions, are cheap to deploy and remain state-of-the-art under temporal drift and in selective classification. Yet, attackers can evade them by adding benign-looking content that outweighs malicious evidence. Canonically, detectors encode the presence of a few thousand features, selected during training, as sparse multi-hot vectors over a fixed vocabulary. Features that emerge after training remain invisible. We show that linear models and multi-layer perceptrons (MLPs) over this input are sum-pooled set models in disguise. Sum-pooling lets added benign features cancel malicious evidence. Instead, we cast malware detection with set-shaped static features as a multiple-instance learning (MIL) problem. To this end, we propose MalSets, which uses max-pooled Deep Sets models with a monotone head to ensure that any malicious evidence remains undiluted; thus, more is never less. Under MIL, a general text encoder maps any feature string to an embedding, thus eliminating the long-standing out-of-vocabulary problem at test time. Max-pooling retains the malicious evidence regardless of how many benign features an attacker adds. Since max-pooling can only grow when features are added, constraining the head alone makes the malware score monotone under additions, even against a white-box attacker adapted to this architecture. While monotone detectors are never evaded by state-of-the-art black-box or white-box attacks, they often significantly pay for this robustness in clean performance since benign features cannot count as evidence. However, by combining a non-monotone set encoder with max-pooling and a monotone head, MalSets maintains the robustness of prior monotone classifiers while achieving state-of-the-art performance.

candidates.title: Statistical mechanics of linear classification on hierarchical tree data
candidates.abstract: Deep networks owe much of their success to their ability to exploit the structure in data, from the grammar of language to the multi-scale organization of images. Yet, many statistical mechanics approaches to structured data rely on Gaussian equivalence, whose assumptions can fail when a few latent variables influence all input coordinates. In this work, we take a step beyond this setting with a simple setup, in which a linear classifier is trained to infer the root of the classical broadcast process on a tree from its $N$ leaves. Despite this simplicity, the data already display non-Gaussian statistics along the direction carrying the label, as well as strong finite-size effects. By retaining the exact law along this direction and approximating the transverse fluctuations as Gaussian, we obtain a finite-depth replica theory that accurately describes the measured learning curves. At large depth and sufficiently weak regularization, we uncover a double descent whose two stages are separated in scale. In a range of broadcast noise below the reconstruction threshold, the first descent occurs at a number of samples scaling as $N^ω$, with $0<ω<1$ set by the data statistics, whereas the overfitting peak occurs at order $N$ samples. Beyond linear classifiers, this setup could serve as a controlled starting point to study deeper architectures and generative models on hierarchical data.

candidates.title: When Being Wrong Is Right: Reverse-Capability Audio CAPTCHAs through Psychoacoustic Design
candidates.abstract: Large audio-language models (LALMs) have recently been shown to bypass audio CAPTCHAs designed around limitations of automatic speech recognition. To address this threat, we introduce reverse-capability verification, a general CAPTCHA framework that reverses the conventional human-easy, machine-hard relationship with respect to the physical ground truth. It selects challenges in which stable human perceptual limitations cause the human-reference answer to differ from the physical ground truth, while machine analysis tends toward that truth. Because the verifier accepts the human-reference answer, advanced solver capabilities and resulting improved recovery of the physical ground truth may instead strengthen the human-machine separation. We instantiate the framework through psychoacoustics and design two audio CAPTCHAs: HIPI, a classification task, and YINGCHEN, a counting task, together with their conjunctive composition. Across seven LALMs and eight attack strategies, the maximum observed machine acceptance rates are 19%, 17%, and 3% for HIPI, YINGCHEN, and their composition, respectively, compared with 45-100% for nine prior schemes. A multidimensional human usability study yields corresponding human acceptance rates of 78%, 90%, and 76%, while maintaining competitive efficiency and satisfaction. Further analysis demonstrates that advanced LALMs tend toward physical ground truth. These results show that reverse-capability verification substantially reduces machine acceptance while retaining high human acceptance through an approach different from conventional CAPTCHAs.

candidates.title: Pixel Auto-Encoder: Reconstructing Language Model Activations Through Pixel Art
candidates.abstract: Interpreting the high-dimensional internal representations of large language models (LLMs) remains a challenging problem. Recent approaches have explored translating these representations into human-understandable forms, particularly natural language. In this work, we explore the use of images as an alternative target modality for interpreting LLM activations. As a first step toward this goal, we introduce Pixel Auto-Encoder, which converts intermediate LLM activations into $32 \times 32$, 32-color pixel art and reconstructs them for subsequent computation within the model. By encouraging the intermediate representations to resemble predefined concept images, we investigate whether LLM activations can be expressed visually while preserving the model's language capabilities. We find that the model can produce target-aligned images for some concepts, and that replacing pixel representations with concept images can influence next-token predictions. However, we also observe a trade-off between visual alignment and language-model performance, as well as sensitivity to pixel-level changes that are difficult to interpret visually. These findings demonstrate the feasibility and limitations of image-based representations of LLM activations.

candidates.title: PointNeXt Adapter Improved Model for BIM Component Defect Association under Construction Images and Design Model Attributes
candidates.abstract: Construction site defect analysis increasingly requires linking field evidence to the correct BIM object, because a crack, spalling area, missing sleeve or misaligned support is useful for quality control only when it is connected with component identity, location, responsibility and design intent. This paper proposes a PointNeXt Adapter improved model for BIM component defect association under construction images and design model attributes. The method aligns site image crops, local point cloud patches, BIM component identifiers, geometry attributes, material categories, installation stage, inspection distance, viewpoint quality and source reliability tags into component level inspection windows. PointNeXt learns local geometry and deviation from as built point evidence, while the adapter injects BIM attributes so the same geometric irregularity can be interpreted differently for structural, envelope, MEP and embedded components. The fusion head outputs component link, defect class, defect probability, confidence, dominant evidence and recommended review action. A synthetic multisource BIM inspection dataset is used to evaluate repeated layouts, occlusion, sparse point clouds, registration errors and unseen component arrangements. Results show that attribute aware point learning improves association accuracy, defect recall and confidence calibration compared with image only, point only, simple fusion and adapter free baselines. The framework is positioned as traceable BIM issue review support, requiring manual confirmation and staged field validation before operational deployment.

candidates.title: Improving semantic equivalence in research-level math formalization
candidates.abstract: Formalizing mathematics in Lean is never a word-for-word translation of a paper: a Lean formalization changes definitions, strengthens hypotheses, splits arguments, and adds lemmas the paper never mentions. It stands to reason that a model that is good at autoformalization must be a good predictor of how a natural language source must differ from its faithful Lean formalization. With that in mind, we collect 4{,}076 audited examples of such changes from 832 Lean projects that formalize research-level mathematics, and use them to ask a practical question: how well can a model \emph{write} Lean inside a real research-level project that may contain tens of thousands of lines of code, and does training on discrepancies between natural language sources and their faithful Lean formalizations help? Our training set consists of 3{,}431 tasks from 141 repositories, and the test set consists of 645 tasks from the remaining 27 repositories. Training on in-project Lean nearly doubles complete proofs ($11\% \to 20\%$) and raises the share of statements in gold agreement with the project's own formalization by nearly a third ($30\%$ to $39\%$). The gain comes from the pairs themselves: an adapter trained only to predict how the Lean will differ, or a model told the difference in advance, barely helps. Training on where formalizations depart from their sources is thus an effective way of improving semantic equivalence in research-level formalization.

candidates.title: ViTrust: Learning 3D Observation Trust for Deformable Physical World Models
candidates.abstract: Learning deformable physical world models requires dynamics that generalize beyond observed motion. Accurate reconstruction alone does not ensure accurate future prediction, motivating us to learn how observations should influence physical identification. However, visual reliability alone does not determine how informative an observation is about physical dynamics. We propose ViTrust to learn 3D observation trust, determining how strongly each tracked point influences physical identification. Its key design is a visual-contact trust adapter that combines pointwise spatiotemporal evidence with interaction history on a persistent contact graph to predict time-varying observation weights. A single-stage, shared-forward objective jointly optimizes these weights and physical parameters through weighted geometry and correspondence losses, with constraints to prevent observation-weight collapse. All learning uses only the observed prefix. The fitted physics remains fixed for future prediction under supplied controls. Experiments on real-world sequences demonstrate improved future prediction over the evaluated baselines, alongside qualitative demonstrations of novel-control rollouts and cross-object transfer.

candidates.title: Beyond Raw IQ: Compact Semantic Representations for Task Oriented Automatic Modulation Classification
candidates.abstract: Automatic modulation classification (AMC) is an important component of modern wireless communication systems, but conventional signal representations can be expensive to store, process, and communicate, particularly under noisy channel conditions. This work investigates whether learned semantic representations can provide a compact alternative to high-dimensional in-phase and quadrature (IQ) representations while retaining robustness to noise. Starting from a 2048-dimensional IQ representation, we evaluate learned semantic representations with dimensions of 4, 8, 16, 32, and 64. Across the evaluated configurations, a 16-dimensional representation provides the strongest overall trade-off between classification performance, robustness, and representation size. The resulting representation achieves a 128x compression ratio and a 99.22% reduction in dimensionality. We further evaluate representation stability across signal-to-noise ratios (SNRs), compare semantic representations with a raw-IQ CNN, analyze per-class robustness, and perform five-seed validation. The five-seed evaluation produces an average accuracy of (49.22 +- 0.52)% and Macro-F1 of (49.27 +- 0.53)% across the evaluated SNR range. These results indicate that learned semantic compression can produce a substan- tially smaller representation while preserving useful classification information and improving geometric stability under noise.

candidates.title: The Humming Revachol: A Dialogue Network Analysis of Narrative Power in Disco Elysium
candidates.abstract: This study applies social network analysis to the narrative RPG Disco Elysium to examine how narrative power is distributed among its characters. A directed, weighted character-mention network of 73 NPCs is constructed from the game's complete dialogue script, with characters identified and annotated across five social attributes. Narrative power is operationalised through four dimensions: attention, authority, discursive initiative, and embeddedness. Non-parametric statistical tests examine differences across gender, age, race, class, and ideology. The findings suggest that narrative power is largely independent of social identity categories and is more closely associated with character narrative functions, while structural embeddedness reflects the socio-organisational contexts in which characters are situated. These findings show that dialogue-network analysis can reveal structural patterns of representation that visibility counts alone would miss.

candidates.title: Learning free energy across a differentiable temperature range by deep generative modeling
candidates.abstract: Free energy governs the directionality, stability, and temperature sensitivity of physical, chemical, and biological transformations. Conventional free energy calculations, such as thermodynamic integration and free energy perturbation, often have to be performed at individual temperatures and are limited by the high cost of sampling an extensive set of thermodynamic states. Here, we introduce learned temperature-differentiable free energy perturbation (TD-FEP), a deep generative framework that learns a temperature-conditioned, invertible mapping between reference and target systems through data-free, energy-based optimization. TD-FEP thereby unifies one-shot state generation and free energy calculation across a continuous temperature range. We validated TD-FEP across a broad range of applications, including isolated molecules, periodic materials, and chemical reactions.

candidates.title: RadAG: Reward-Adversarial Attention Guidance for Efficient Inference-Time Alignment of Diffusion Models
candidates.abstract: Diffusion and flow-based models have achieved remarkable success in generation, yet their samples often remain suboptimal in fidelity and text alignment. Two lines of inference-time methods address this: extrapolation guidance, such as classifier-free guidance (CFG) and its variants, and reward guidance, which aligns samples with reward models of human preference. Extrapolation guidance needs only forward passes, but it builds its reference by heuristic rules unrelated to the reward and therefore cannot steer sampling toward a given reward. Gradient-based reward guidance steers sampling directly toward a higher reward, but backpropagates through the entire generator at every step. This trade-off raises the question of whether extrapolation guidance can steer sampling toward a higher reward without a full backward pass. To answer this, we introduce Reward-Adversarial Attention Guidance (RadAG), which constructs the reference by perturbing the attention logits of a single block against their reward gradient and extrapolates away from it. We prove that this update increases the reward of the clean estimate to first order, while its backward pass stops at the perturbed block instead of traversing the entire generator. On FLUX.2-klein-4B and 9B with PickScore and aesthetic rewards, RadAG achieves the highest target reward in every setting with 30-65% less time than gradient-based and candidate-based baselines.

candidates.title: When do stored facts become available in looped transformers?
candidates.abstract: Looped transformers do not acquire new knowledge during a forward pass. Prior work shows that they store as many bits in their weights as non-looped models. It remains unclear how recurrence makes this knowledge available during inference. We study this question using synthetic factual recall and multi-hop reasoning, measuring depth-resolved readable information in bits with native readouts and tuned lenses. Under final-loop supervision, single-hop facts become readable progressively: heavier memorization loads delay retrieval despite comparable final readable information. Untied baselines of equal unrolled depth concentrate retrieval near the end of their stacks, whereas looped models expose facts earlier. This delay is not intrinsic to the tested recall tasks: training with supervision and depth-specific readouts at every loop makes near-final information readable after the first loop in all tested configurations. Representational analysis shows value-related structure emerging within states organized by the query key. We then study multi-hop chains whose facts are stored in the weights rather than given in the prompt. Intermediate entities become decodable in chain order, and aligned transitions show next-entity structure developing while current-entity structure remains dominant. Interventions in a released six-recurrence model establish a causal role for these representations. Counterfactual replacements of a probe-defined entity component at a single prompt position redirect downstream bridge entities and the final answer. Conversely, replacements from queries that reach the same entity through different preceding relations, preserving the remaining relation suffix, retain the original answer in over 99.5\% of tested cases. These results distinguish a training-dependent schedule for factual recall from the causal role of retrieved-entity representations in subsequent composition.

candidates.title: Synthetic EHR Generators Should Be Audited Like LLMs
candidates.abstract: Synthetic electronic health record (EHR) generation is increasingly adopting large autoregressive models, yet privacy evaluation has not kept pace, relying heavily on similarity-based heuristics and aggregate metrics that can obscure patient-specific memorisation. We argue that these models should additionally undergo LLM-style memorisation audits at the level of individual patient records. We support this position by comparing membership-inference evaluations across four prominent autoregressive EHR generators, highlighting inconsistent evaluation practices in patient representations and attack procedures. We evaluate trajectory reconstruction from partial context and introduce randomly assigned patient-level canaries to distinguish memorised associations from clinical generalisation. We examine these methods in a GPT-2-style model deliberately overfit to 1,000 MIMIC-IV patient trajectories, creating a controlled setting in which memorisation should be readily detectable. The model systematically recovers training patients' canaries, and their trajectory reconstruction approaches perfect accuracy with increasing context. Held-out patients show no systematic canary recovery, while reconstruction remains low and improves only marginally with additional context. These experiments establish a positive-control baseline for further evaluation of these methods in realistically trained models.

candidates.title: Not All Directions Are Flat: Decomposed-Gradient Flatness for Sparse-View 3D Gaussian Splatting
candidates.abstract: Many applications of novel view synthesis, such as augmented reality and robotics, can afford only a few input views, since dense capture is costly. With such sparse views, however, 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) overfits the training views and degrades at unseen viewpoints. Among the approaches to this problem, flat-minima optimization treats the Gaussians as trainable parameters and steers training toward flat minima, which generalize better, by perturbing the Gaussians with random noise or along the training gradient. However, these perturbations ignore their direction relative to the other training views. Interestingly, we find that the direction of the perturbation determines whether it improves generalization. Specifically, we decompose the gradient of each training view into a component parallel to the average gradient of all views, on which the views agree, and an orthogonal component, on which they disagree. Perturbing along the orthogonal component improves generalization, whereas perturbing along the parallel component does not. We further find that the flatness correction often opposes the reconstruction gradient, shrinking or even reversing the reconstruction step. Based on these findings, we propose DecoFlat, which perturbs each Gaussian along the orthogonal component together with random noise. Furthermore, we introduce a conflict-aware correction, which removes the part of the flatness correction that opposes the reconstruction gradient, and a rescheduling of the spherical-harmonics color, which suppresses the overfitting of view-dependent appearance. Extensive experiments demonstrate that DecoFlat, as a plug-in optimizer, consistently improves vanilla 3DGS and a wide range of sparse-view 3DGS methods.

candidates.title: HighwayVerse: A Chain-of-Inspection Benchmark for Highway Infrastructure Anomaly Understanding
candidates.abstract: Practical highway infrastructure inspection entails progressive diagnostic reasoning from visual perception to maintenance decisions, yet existing benchmarks remain confined to isolated tasks, leaving Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) insufficiently evaluated across sequential inspection stages.
